sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>
sections.docs:
<docs>
Pi documentation (read only when the user asks about pi itself, its SDK, extensions, themes, skills, or TUI):
- Main documentation: <vol>/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/README.md
- Additional docs: <vol>/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs
- Examples: <vol>/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples (extensions, custom tools, SDK)
- When reading pi docs or examples, resolve docs/... under Additional docs and examples/... under Examples, not the current working directory
- When asked about: extensions (docs/extensions.md, examples/extensions/), themes (docs/themes.md), skills (docs/skills.md), prompt templates (docs/prompt-templates.md), TUI components (docs/tui.md), keybindings (docs/keybindings.md), SDK integrations (docs/sdk.md), custom providers (docs/custom-provider.md), adding models (docs/models.md), pi packages (docs/packages.md), environment variables (docs/environment-variables.md), MCP servers (docs/mcp.md), codemode scripts and non-LLM models such as classifiers and image models (docs/codemode.md)
- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing
- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)
</docs>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Create an animated, non-interactive surfing pelican using html/3js

Build this as an interactive web page in the current directory.
- The entry point is index.html. Put your code in JavaScript ES modules loaded from it
  (`<script type="module" src="main.js">`), and add a short README.md.
- You may use npm packages: `npm install <package>` here, then import them by name
  (`import * as THREE from "three"`). No CDN URLs and no import maps.
- Afterwards the page is packaged into one self-contained index.html with esbuild: every script and
  stylesheet index.html references is bundled with everything it imports. Load assets the page needs
  with `import` (they become data URLs) or generate them in code, never by URL string.
- The packaged page runs offline in a sandboxed iframe: no network requests, and no localStorage,
  cookies or other storage (they throw there).
- Check that it packages: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` must succeed.
  Don't build or package the page yourself; that happens afterwards.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

vec2 waveGrad(vec2 p, float t){

}

// Shared wave field: identical math in JS (for floating objects) and GLSL (for the ocean surface).

export const WAVES = [
  { dir: [1, 0], lambda: 30, speed: 2.4, amp: 1.5, phase: 0 },        // main swell
  { dir: [1, 0], lambda: 15, speed: 2.4, amp: 0.5, phase: -1.1 },      // crest sharpening harmonic
  { dir: [0.83, 0.56], lambda: 22, speed: 1.9, amp: 0.55, phase: 2.1 }, // secondary swell
  { dir: [0.94, -0.34], lambda: 9, speed: 1.6, amp: 0.28, phase: 0.7 },
  { dir: [0.6, -0.8], lambda: 5.8, speed: 1.4, amp: 0.16, phase: 4.0 },
];

// precompute
const TWO_PI = Math.PI * 2;
for (const w of WAVES) {
  const len = Math.hypot(w.dir[0], w.dir[1]);
  w.dx = w.dir[0] / len; w.dz = w.dir[1] / len;
  w.k = TWO_PI / w.lambda;
  w.om = w.k * w.speed;
  w.ph = w.phase;
}

export const SWELL = WAVES[0];

export function waveHeight(x, z, t) {
  let h = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < WAVES.length; i++) {
    const w = WAVES[i];
    h += w.amp * Math.sin((w.dx * x + w.dz * z) * w.k - w.om * t + w.ph);
  }
  return h;
}

export function waveNormal(x, z, t, out) {
  let gx = 0, gz = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < WAVES.length; i++) {
    const w = WAVES[i];
    const c = w.amp * w.k * Math.cos((w.dx * x + w.dz * z) * w.k - w.om * t + w.ph);
    gx += w.dx * c; gz += w.dz * c;
  }
  out.set(-gx, 1, -gz).normalize();
  return out;
}

      uHorizon: { value: new THREE.Color(PALETTE.horizon) },

      varying vec3 vDir;
      void main() {
        vDir = position;
        gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
      }
    `,
    fragmentShader: `
      uniform vec3 uZenith; uniform vec3 uHorizon; uniform vec3 uSunColor; uniform vec3 uSunDir;
      varying vec3 vDir;
      void main() {
        vec3 d = normalize(vDir);
        float h = max(d.y, 0.0);
        vec3 col = mix(uHorizon, uZenith, pow(h, 0.55));
        float s = max(dot(d, normalize(uSunDir)), 0.0);

        gl_FragColor = vec4(col, 1.0);
        #include <tonemapping_fragment>
        #include <colorspace_fragment>
      }

function pulse(t, period, dur, phase = 0) {
  const x = ((t / period + phase) % 1) * period;  // time since last pulse start
  if (x > dur) return 0;
  const u = x / dur;
  return Math.sin(u * Math.PI) ** 2; // smooth in-out
}

import * as THREE from 'three';
import { PALETTE } from './theme.js';
import { glslWaveChunk } from './waves.js';

export function createOcean(sunDir) {
  const geo = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(560, 560, 380, 380);
  geo.rotateX(-Math.PI / 2);
  const uniforms = {
    uTime: { value: 0 },
    uSunDir: { value: sunDir.clone() },
    uCamPos: { value: new THREE.Vector3() },
    uDeep: { value: new THREE.Color(PALETTE.waterDeep) },
    uShallow: { value: new THREE.Color(PALETTE.waterShallow) },
    uSkyTint: { value: new THREE.Color(PALETTE.waterSky) },
    uSun: { value: new THREE.Color(PALETTE.sun) },
    uFog: { value: new THREE.Color(PALETTE.fog) },
  };
  const mat = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
    uniforms,
    vertexShader: /* glsl */`
      uniform float uTime;
      varying vec3 vWorld;
      varying vec3 vN;
      varying float vH;
      ${glslWaveChunk()}
      void main() {
        vec4 wp = modelMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
        float h = waveH(wp.xz, uTime);
        wp.y += h;
        vec2 g = waveGrad(wp.xz, uTime);
        vN = normalize(vec3(-g.x, 1.0, -g.y));
        vH = h;
        vWorld = wp.xyz;
        gl_Position = projectionMatrix * viewMatrix * wp;
      }
    `,
    fragmentShader: /* glsl */`
      uniform float uTime;
      uniform vec3 uSunDir, uCamPos, uDeep, uShallow, uSkyTint, uSun, uFog;
      varying vec3 vWorld;
      varying vec3 vN;
      varying float vH;
      void main() {
        vec2 p = vWorld.xz;
        float t = uTime;
        vec3 N = normalize(vN);
        // fine ripples (normals only)
        float th1 = dot(vec2(0.85, 0.53), p) * 2.4166 - 2.6583 * t;
        float th2 = dot(vec2(0.28, -0.96), p) * 3.6959 - 3.6959 * t + 1.7;
        float th3 = dot(vec2(-0.60, 0.80), p) * 6.9813 - 6.2831 * t + 3.9;
        vec2 g = vec2(0.0);
        g += vec2(0.85, 0.53) * (0.045 * 2.4166 * cos(th1));
        g += vec2(0.28, -0.96) * (0.030 * 3.6959 * cos(th2));
        g += vec2(-0.60, 0.80) * (0.018 * 6.9813 * cos(th3));
        N = normalize(N + vec3(-g.x, 0.0, -g.y) * 1.5);
        vec3 V = normalize(uCamPos - vWorld);
        float fres = pow(1.0 - max(dot(N, V), 0.0), 3.0);
        vec3 col = mix(uDeep, uShallow, clamp((vH + 1.3) * 0.32, 0.0, 1.0));
        col = mix(col, uSkyTint, clamp(fres * 0.65, 0.0, 1.0));
        vec3 R = reflect(-normalize(uSunDir), N);
        float sparkle = 0.55 + 0.45 * sin(th1 * 3.7 + th2 * 2.9);
        float spec = pow(max(dot(R, V), 0.0), 150.0) * (1.4 + 2.2 * sparkle);
        col += uSun * spec;
        // foam
        float n = sin(p.x * 0.55 + p.y * 0.35 - t * 0.9) * sin(p.y * 0.62 - p.x * 0.28 + t * 0.7);
        n += 0.6 * sin(p.x * 1.31 - p.y * 0.77 + t * 1.3);
        float crest = smoothstep(1.28, 1.95, vH);
        float steep = clamp(length(vN.xz) * 1.8, 0.0, 1.0);
        float foam = crest * clamp(0.30 + 0.55 * n, 0.0, 1.0) + crest * steep * 0.55;
        foam = clamp(foam, 0.0, 1.0);
        col = mix(col, vec3(0.93, 0.97, 0.96), foam * 0.85);
        // horizon fog
        float dist = distance(uCamPos, vWorld);
        col = mix(col, uFog, smoothstep(80.0, 235.0, dist));
        gl_FragColor = vec4(col, 1.0);
        #include <tonemapping_fragment>
        #include <colorspace_fragment>
      }
    `,
  });
  const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat);
  mesh.frustumCulled = false;
  return { mesh, uniforms };
}

```js
// The wave field, shared bit-for-bit between JS (floating objects) and GLSL (ocean surface).

export const WAVES = [
  { dir: [1, 0], lambda: 30, speed: 2.4, amp: 1.5, phase: 0 },        // the swell the pelican rides
  { dir: [1, 0], lambda: 15, speed: 2.4, amp: 0.5, phase: -1.1 },      // sharpens the crest
  { dir: [0.83, 0.56], lambda: 22, speed: 1.9, amp: 0.55, phase: 2.1 },// crossing swell
  { dir: [0.94, -0.34], lambda: 11, speed: 1.6, amp: 0.26, phase: 0.7 },// chop
  { dir: [0.6, -0.8], lambda: 7, speed: 1.4, amp: 0.14, phase: 4.0 }, // finer chop
];

const TAU = Math.PI * 2;
for (const w of WAVES) {
  const l = Math.hypot(w.dir[0], w.dir[1]) || 1;
  w.dx = w.dir[0] / l;
  w.dz = w.dir[1] / l;
  w.k = TAU / w.lambda;
  w.om = w.k * w.speed;
}

export const SWELL = WAVES[0];

export function waveHeight(x, z, t) {
  let h = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < WAVES.length; i++) {
    const w = WAVES[i];
    h += w.amp * Math.sin((w.dx * x + w.dz * z) * w.k - w.om * t + w.phase);
  }
  return h;
}

export function waveNormal(x, z, t, out) {
  let gx = 0, gz = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < WAVES.length; i++) {
    const w = WAVES[i];
    const c = w.amp * w.k * Math.cos((w.dx * x + w.dz * z) * w.k - w.om * t + w.phase);
    gx += w.dx * c;
    gz += w.dz * c;
  }
  return out.set(-gx, 1, -gz).normalize();
}

function fmt(n) {
  let s = n.toFixed(6).replace(/(\.\d*?)0+$/, '$1');
  if (s.endsWith('.')) s = s.slice(0, -1);
  if (!/[.eE]/.test(s)) s += '.0';
  return s === '-0.0' ? '0.0' : s;
}
```

```js
export function glslWaveChunk() {
  let hf = 'float waveH(vec2 p, float t) {\n  float h = 0.0;\n';
  let gf = 'vec2 waveGrad(vec2 p, float t) {\n  vec2 g = vec2(0.0);\n';
  for (const w of WAVES) {
    const th = `dot(vec2(${fmt(w.dx)}, ${fmt(w.dz)}), p) * ${fmt(w.k)} - ${fmt(w.om)} * t + (${fmt(w.phase)})`;
    hf += `  h += ${fmt(w.amp)} * sin(${th});\n`;
    gf += `  g += vec2(${fmt(w.dx)}, ${fmt(w.dz)}) * (${fmt(w.amp * w.k)} * cos(${th}));\n`;
  }
  hf += '  return h;\n}\n\n';
  gf += '  return g;\n}\n';
  return hf + gf;
}
```

export function makeGlowTexture(stops, size = 128) {
  const c = document.createElement('canvas');
  c.width = c.height = size;

function mat(color, opts = {}) {
  return new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: new THREE.Color(color), roughness: 0.62, ...opts });
}

function pulse(t, period, dur, phase = 0) {
  const x = ((((t / period + phase) % 1) + 1) % 1) * period;
  if (x >= dur) return 0;
  const u = x / dur;
  return Math.sin(u * Math.PI) ** 2;
}

export function createPelican() {
  const board = new THREE.Group();

    const u = (x + 1.65) / 3.5;

  function update(ctx) {
    const t = ctx.t;
    const dt = ctx.dt;

    pel.rotation.y = 0.14 * Math.sin(0.13 * t) + ctx.lean * 0.12;

    body.position.y = 0.72 + 0.03 * Math.sin(2.2 * t) - ctx.crouch * 0.10;
    body.rotation.z = -0.16 - ctx.crouch * 0.10 + ctx.lean * 0.30;
    body.rotation.x = ctx.lean * 0.38;

    const burst = pulse(t, 8.5, 1.9, 0.35);
    const flapA = 0.32 + 0.05 * Math.sin(1.4 * t) + burst * 0.5 * Math.sin(11 * t);
    for (const w of wings) {
      w.flap.rotation.x = -w.s * flapA;
      w.elbow.rotation.x = w.s * (0.30 + burst * 0.28 * Math.sin(11 * t - 0.9));
      w.shoulder.rotation.y = -w.s * (0.55 + Math.abs(ctx.lean) * 0.18);
    }

    const gulp = pulse(t, 7.3, 1.3, 0.6);
    jaw.rotation.z = -0.55 * gulp;
    pouch.scale.set(2.3 * (1 + 0.10 * gulp), 1.0 * (1 + 0.55 * gulp), 0.8 * (1 + 0.16 * gulp));

    if (ctx.fishWorld) {
      head.getWorldPosition(_v1);
      head.parent.getWorldQuaternion(_q1).invert();
      _v2.copy(ctx.fishWorld).sub(_v1).normalize().applyQuaternion(_q1);
      const ang = Math.acos(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(_v2.x, -1, 1));

        _v3.crossVectors(X_AXIS, _v2);
        if (_v3.lengthSq() < 1e-8) _v3.set(0, 1, 0); else _v3.normalize();
        _q2.setFromAxisAngle(_v3, 1.15);

export function createSpray() {
  const CAP = 800;
  const pos = new Float32Array(CAP * 3);
  const vel = new Float32Array(CAP * 3);
  const size = new Float32Array(CAP);
  const alpha = new Float32Array(CAP);
  const age = new Float32Array(CAP);
  const life = new Float32Array(CAP);
  let alive = 0;

  const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
  geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(pos, 3).setUsage(THREE.DynamicDrawUsage));
  geo.setAttribute('aSize', new THREE.BufferAttribute(size, 1).setUsage(THREE.DynamicDrawUsage));
  geo.setAttribute('aAlpha', new THREE.BufferAttribute(alpha, 1).setUsage(THREE.DynamicDrawUsage));
  geo.setDrawRange(0, 0);

  const mat = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
    transparent: true,
    depthWrite: false,
    uniforms: {
      uColor: { value: new THREE.Color(PALETTE.foam) },
      uScale: { value: 900 },
    },
    vertexShader: /* glsl */ `
      attribute float aSize;
      attribute float aAlpha;
      uniform float uScale;
      varying float vA;
      void main() {
        vA = aAlpha;
        vec4 mv = modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
        gl_PointSize = aSize * uScale / max(0.3, -mv.z);
        gl_Position = projectionMatrix * mv;
      }
    `,
    fragmentShader: /* glsl */ `
      uniform vec3 uColor;
      varying float vA;
      void main() {
        float d = length(gl_PointCoord - vec2(0.5));
        float a = (1.0 - smoothstep(0.18, 0.5, d)) * vA;
        if (a < 0.01) discard;
        gl_FragColor = vec4(uColor, a);
        #include <tonemapping_fragment>
        #include <colorspace_fragment>
      }
    `,
  });

  const points = new THREE.Points(geo, mat);
  points.frustumCulled = false;

  function copySlot(i, j) {
    for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) {
      pos[i * 3 + k] = pos[j * 3 + k];
      vel[i * 3 + k] = vel[j * 3 + k];
    }
    size[i] = size[j];
    alpha[i] = alpha[j];
    age[i] = age[j];
    life[i] = life[j];
  }

  const _p = new THREE.Vector3();
  const _v = new THREE.Vector3();

  function spawn(p, v, s, l) {
    if (alive >= CAP) return;
    const i = alive++;
    pos[i * 3] = p.x; pos[i * 3 + 1] = p.y; pos[i * 3 + 2] = p.z;
    vel[i * 3] = v.x; vel[i * 3 + 1] = v.y; vel[i * 3 + 2] = v.z;
    size[i] = s; age[i] = 0; life[i] = l; alpha[i] = 0;
  }

  function burst(p, n, opts = {}) {
    const spread = opts.spread ?? 1.5;
    const up = opts.up ?? 2.6;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      const a = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2;
      const r = Math.random();
      _p.set(p.x + Math.cos(a) * r * spread, p.y, p.z + Math.sin(a) * r * spread);
      _v.set(Math.cos(a) * (0.4 + Math.random()), up * (0.4 + Math.random() * 0.8), Math.sin(a) * (0.4 + Math.random()));
      spawn(_p, _v, (opts.size ?? 0.15) * (0.6 + Math.random() * 0.9), (opts.life ?? 0.8) * (0.6 + Math.random() * 0.8));
    }
  }

  function update(dt, t) {
    let n = alive;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; ) {
      age[i] += dt;
      if (age[i] >= life[i]) { n--; if (i !== n) copySlot(i, n); continue; }
      vel[i * 3 + 1] -= 7.5 * dt;
      pos[i * 3] += vel[i * 3] * dt;
      pos[i * 3 + 1] += vel[i * 3 + 1] * dt;
      pos[i * 3 + 2] += vel[i * 3 + 2] * dt;
      if (pos[i * 3 + 1] < waveHeight(pos[i * 3], pos[i * 3 + 2], t) - 0.06) {
        n--; if (i !== n) copySlot(i, n); continue;
      }
      const u = age[i] / life[i];
      alpha[i] = 0.85 * Math.sin(Math.min(u, 1) * Math.PI);
      i++;
    }
    alive = n;
    geo.setDrawRange(0, n);
    geo.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true;
    geo.attributes.aSize.needsUpdate = true;
    geo.attributes.aAlpha.needsUpdate = true;
  }

  function setScale(height, fovDeg) {
    mat.uniforms.uScale.value = height / (2 * Math.tan((fovDeg * Math.PI) / 360));
  }

  return { points, spawn, burst, update, setScale };
}

// distant scenery follows the rider

const pelican = createPelican();

scene.add(spray.points);

const fish = createFishFX();

// scratch objects
const _n = new THREE.Vector3();
const _f = new THREE.Vector3();
const _r = new THREE.Vector3();
const _u = new THREE.Vector3();
const _camPos = new THREE.Vector3();
const _look = new THREE.Vector3();
const _spawn = new THREE.Vector3();
const _vel = new THREE.Vector3();
const _m = new THREE.Matrix4();
const _q = new THREE.Quaternion();
const AXIS_X = new THREE.Vector3(1, 0, 0);
const AXIS_Z = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 1);
const camLook = new THREE.Vector3(12, 1, 2);

const clock = new THREE.Clock();
let t = 0;
let sprayAcc = 0;

function frame() {
  const dt = Math.min(clock.getDelta(), 0.05);
  t += dt;

  // ── pelican kinematics: hold position on the face of the traveling swell while carving ──
  const xBase = (THETA_FACE + SWELL.om * t - SWELL.phase) / SWELL.k;
  const x = xBase + 0.9 * Math.sin(0.19 * t + 0.6);
  const z = 6.2 * Math.sin(0.12 * t) + 2.4 * Math.sin(0.29 * t + 1.7);
  const z1 = 6.2 * 0.12 * Math.cos(0.12 * t) + 2.4 * 0.29 * Math.cos(0.29 * t + 1.7);
  const z2 = -6.2 * 0.0144 * Math.sin(0.12 * t) - 2.4 * 0.0841 * Math.sin(0.29 * t + 1.7);
  const vx = SWELL.speed + 0.9 * 0.19 * Math.cos(0.19 * t + 0.6);
  const speed = Math.hypot(vx, z1);
  const carve = THREE.MathUtils.clamp(z1 / 0.9, -1, 1);
  const lean = THREE.MathUtils.clamp(z2 * 2.6, -0.6, 0.6);
  const crouch = 0.5 + 0.5 * Math.sin(0.4 * t + 1.0);
  const y = waveHeight(x, z, t);

  pelican.board.position.set(x, y + 0.06, z);
  waveNormal(x, z, t, _n);
  _f.set(vx, 0, z1).normalize();
  _f.addScaledVector(_n, -_f.dot(_n)).normalize();
  _r.crossVectors(_f, _n).normalize();
  _u.crossVectors(_r, _f).normalize();
  _m.makeBasis(_f, _u, _r);
  pelican.board.quaternion.setFromRotationMatrix(_m);
  _q.setFromAxisAngle(AXIS_X, lean);       // heel into the turn
  pelican.board.quaternion.multiply(_q);
  _q.setFromAxisAngle(AXIS_Z, 0.05 * Math.sin(0.9 * t));  // gentle trim
  pelican.board.quaternion.multiply(_q);

  pelican.update({ t, dt, carve, lean, crouch, fishWorld: fish.active() });

  // ── spray ──
  sprayAcc += dt * (26 + Math.abs(lean) * 130 + Math.max(0, speed - 2.3) * 60 + Math.abs(carve) * 24);
  const emit = Math.floor(sprayAcc);
  sprayAcc -= emit;
  for (let i = 0; i < emit; i++) {
    pelican.nose.getWorldPosition(_spawn);
    _spawn.x += (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.3;
    _spawn.z += (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.3;
    _vel.set(
      vx * 0.28 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.8,
      1.2 + Math.random() * 2.2,
      z1 * 0.28 - lean * 2.2 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 1.4
    );
    spray.spawn(_spawn, _vel, 0.05 + Math.random() * 0.13, 0.45 + Math.random() * 0.55);
  }
  if (Math.abs(lean) > 0.22 && Math.random() < dt * 45) {
    (lean > 0 ? pelican.railR : pelican.railL).getWorldPosition(_spawn);
    _vel.set(vx * 0.2, 1.6 + Math.random() * 2, -lean * 3 + (Math.random() - 0.5));
    spray.spawn(_spawn, _vel, 0.08 + Math.random() * 0.16, 0.5 + Math.random() * 0.5);
  }
  spray.update(dt, t);

  fish.update(dt, t, pelican.board.position, spray);
  gulls.update(t);
  clouds.update(dt);

  // ── world follows the rider ──
  rig.position.set(x, 0, z);
  ocean.mesh.position.set(x, 0, z);

  // ── camera ──
  _camPos.set(x - 4.8, y + 2.4, z + 4.6 + 1.6 * Math.sin(0.05 * t));
  const minY = waveHeight(_camPos.x, _camPos.z, t) + 0.6;
  if (_camPos.y < minY) _camPos.y = minY;
  camera.position.lerp(_camPos, 1 - Math.exp(-2.2 * dt));
  _look.set(x + 1.8, y + 1.05, z + 0.4 * Math.sin(0.05 * t));
  camLook.lerp(_look, 1 - Math.exp(-3 * dt));
  camera.lookAt(camLook);

  ocean.uniforms.uTime.value = t;
  ocean.uniforms.uCamPos.value.copy(camera.position);

  renderer.render(scene, camera);
}

function onResize() {
  const w = window.innerWidth;
  const h = window.innerHeight;
  camera.aspect = w / h;
  camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
  renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2));
  renderer.setSize(w, h);
  spray.setScale(h, 50);
}
window.addEventListener('resize', onResize);
onResize();

renderer.setAnimationLoop(frame);

# Surf's up, pelican 🌊

An animated, deliberately **non-interactive** three.js scene: a big-billed
pelican surfing a rolling swell at dawn. Sit back and watch — there is nothing
to click, and that's the point.

## What you'll see

- A pelican riding the **face of a traveling swell** (it holds a fixed phase on
  the wave, so it moves with the wave like a real surfer), carving lazy S-turns
  across it, pumping up and down the face, and heeling into each turn.
- Balance behavior: half-open wings with a constant shimmy and occasional
  takeoff-style **flap bursts**, tail wag, crouch pumping, a bobbing head.
- The famous beak: the jaw hinges open now and then and the **pouch stretches**.
- A leash line from the tail plug to its ankle, spray off the nose and rails,
  whitecap foam on the crests, a glittering sun path, drifting clouds, three
  circling gulls — and a fish that leaps out of the sea now and then (the
  pelican turns its head to watch it).
- A low, cinematic chase camera that never asks you for input.

## How it works

- `waves.js` defines the wave field **once** and shares it bit-for-bit between
  JavaScript (so the board, camera and droplets sit exactly on the surface) and
  GLSL (so the ocean mesh is displaced by the same math, generated from the
  same constants via `glslWaveChunk()`).
- The ocean is one large displaced plane with analytic normals, fragment-level
  ripple normals, crest/face foam, fresnel sky reflection, sun glitter and warm
  distance haze matching the sky shader's horizon.
- The pelican and board are built entirely from primitives (lathe, spheres,
  capsules, boxes, a tube neck, a bezier curve) — no model files.
- Everything is procedural: textures (sun glow, clouds) are drawn to canvases
  in code, so the page makes **zero network requests** and uses no storage —
  safe for offline, sandboxed iframes.
- The "scenery rig" (sky dome, sun, clouds, gulls) follows the rider, so the
  horizon behaves like a truly distant backdrop while the pelican travels.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html` | Entry point; loads `main.js` as an ES module, overlay titles |
| `main.js` | Renderer, scene, kinematics (riding the swell), camera, loop |
| `waves.js` | Shared wave math (JS + GLSL code generation) |
| `ocean.js` | Ocean shader (displacement, foam, glitter, haze) |
| `sky.js` | Sky dome shader + sun glow sprite |
| `pelican.js` | Procedural pelican + surfboard rig and all pose animation |
| `effects.js` | Spray particles, gulls, clouds, jumping fish |
| `theme.js` | Dawn color palette |
| `textures.js` | Canvas-generated textures |

## Run / verify

```sh
npm install

# the packaging check the harness runs — must succeed:
npx esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null
```

To preview locally, bundle once and point the `<script>` tag at the output
(browsers can't resolve the bare `three` import without a bundler):

```sh
npx esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=dev.js
# then temporarily change src="main.js" to src="dev.js" in index.html
```

The final self-contained `index.html` is produced by the packaging step that
runs after this; nothing here needs to be built by hand.

## Summary

I built **"Surf's up, pelican"** — an animated, deliberately non-interactive three.js scene of a pelican surfing a dawn swell.

**The scene:** A pelican (built entirely from primitives — lathe longboard, ellipsoid body, bezier-tube S-neck, hinged beak with a stretchy pouch, articulated wings with dark primaries) rides the steep face of a traveling swell. It holds a fixed phase on the wave like a real surfer, so it genuinely moves with the wave while carving lazy S-turns: heeling into turns, crouch-pumping up and down the face, balancing with half-open wings that shimmy and occasionally burst into full flaps, wagging its tail, and gulping with its pouch. A leash line sags from the tail plug to its ankle, spray flies off the nose and rails (harder mid-turn), whitecap foam streaks the crests, and a fish leaps out of the sea now and then — the pelican turns its head to watch it. Three gulls circle, clouds drift, and a low chase camera sweeps in cinematically and then just follows.

**Key technical points:**
- `waves.js` defines the wave field **once**, shared bit-for-bit between JS (board, camera clamp, droplet landings) and GLSL (auto-generated shader code from the same constants) — so floating objects sit exactly on the shader-displaced ocean
- Custom ocean shader: analytic normals, fragment-level ripple sparkle, crest/face foam, fresnel sky reflection, sun glitter, horizon haze that seamlessly matches the sky-dome gradient
- Everything is procedural (canvas-drawn cloud/glow textures) — zero network requests, no storage, sandbox-safe
- `npx esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` succeeds (1.2 MB bundle)

**Files:** `index.html` (entry + overlay titles), `main.js` (scene/kinematics/camera), `waves.js`, `ocean.js`, `sky.js`, `pelican.js`, `effects.js` (spray, gulls, clouds, fish), `theme.js`, `textures.js`, plus `README.md`.
